newsitem.title: USA: U.S. govt starts effort to find missing pensioners.
newsitem.headline: U.S. govt starts effort to find missing pensioners.

text.p: A U.S. government agency on Tuesday said it was launching an effort to locate workers who have earned private pension benefits but are unaware that they are owed them.

The Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC), a federal corporation that aims to guarantee payment of pensions, launched the "Pension Search Directory" on the Internet that will contain the names of people sought, the name and location of the companies and the date their pension plans ended.

U.S. Labor Secretary Robert Reich, who chairs the PBGC's Board of Directors, said in a statement there are nearly 3,000 Americans who earned a combined total of $10 million in pension benefits but don't know it.
The benefit values range in size but on average, they are about $3,700 per person, he said.
People listed in the directory worked for 565 companies. Most of them are in the airline, steel transportation, machinery, retail trade, apparel and financial services industries.
The directory can be accessed under the Labor Department's home page at www.dol.gov or at http://search.pbgc.gov.
